objective: Add a duplicate and already-answered check at intake that scores a new proposal's objective against every open AND closed docket item and against the records its citations point at, because the lookback measured this class as a larger win than either ranking change and neither ranking can see it
rationale: This proposal is filed on the strength of a measurement that was not the lookback's purpose and turned out to matter more than its verdict. Grading all 114 closed docket items by what they delivered, 13 scored at the bottom of the scale, and they are not thirteen different failures: they are overwhelmingly one shape, work that was ALREADY DONE or already filed when the item was created. w5-tmr-iteration-caps-are-guesses-not-measurements was closed on a reading rather than a rewrite because the commit that did all three things it asked for landed fifteen minutes before the item was drafted. w8-in-sample-inversion-clause was already closed when the pass reached it. w5-figures-must-show-every-rung was already satisfied when checked. w3-refit-stored-studies-in-place, w3-dimension-decides-one-thing, w5-disclose-the-bump-claim and w3-a-study-with-no-rungs all opened by correcting their own premise. And two of the four challenge-kind items in the entire closed cohort, w5-sparta-is-still-the-cheapest-real-result and w5-sparta-frozen-rans-is-the-unblock, are duplicate filings of the same SpaRTA rung that both closed by pointing at the same existing record and spending zero of their 60 core-minute budgets. The decisive point for a ranking argument is that NEITHER candidate ranking can see any of this. Is this already done is not a function of source kind, of estimated cost, or of the entropy of the pre-declared outcomes, so the gain table and the EIG numerator are equally blind to the largest identified waste class in the cohort, and the lookback says so in its own adversarial section rather than leaving it for a reader to notice. Roughly 11 percent of closed items against a numerator change worth rho +0.197 is not a close comparison. The check has an obvious precedent in the tree: the docket already deduplicates proposals by normalized objective text at merge, which catches only exact restatements, and the twelve-dismissals reading already established that ten of twelve dismissed proposals were generated rather than written, four of them sharing a last sentence verbatim from a stored ladder verdict and six opening with the same phrase from a mission report's next-steps prose. Generated proposals are exactly the population a similarity check catches. Axis A: capability-kind at zero solver cost. Axis B: 0. Axis C: 0.
citations: The EIG ranking lookback of 2026-08-10, its adversarial section, which measured the 13 items and named this class the larger win
The docket reading of the twelve dismissed proposals and its generated-rather-than-written finding
The existing deduplication by normalized objective text in the agenda ranking module's merge
The goals and research proposal charter, version 1.4, section 7
The docket item that found a saturated compute window closed nothing, and the gate it found already met
cost_basis: measured; the corpus is the docket and the records already on disk, the check is string and citation comparison with no model and no embedding service, and the retrospective replays it against 114 closed items whose answers are known
expected_knowledge_gain: Two distinguishable outcomes, both of which change how the docket is filed. One: replayed against the closed record the check flags a usable share of the 13 already-done items BEFORE they would have been worked, at a false-positive rate low enough to run at intake, in which case the lab has converted its largest measured source of wasted docket attention into a refusal and the ranking argument becomes the second-order question it should always have been. Two: the check cannot separate them from legitimate follow-ons without flagging so much that nobody would read it, which is itself worth knowing precisely, because it would say the already-done class is not detectable from proposal text and must be caught by the drafter's own citation discipline instead, and it would point the remedy at the generated-proposal pipeline rather than at intake.
in_sample_verdict: The retrospective is run against outcomes that are already known, so the threshold must be frozen BEFORE the replay or the check will be tuned to the 13 cases it is graded on. The gate below requires that ordering explicitly. Nothing else is fitted, no test data is read and no scored column moves.
sequencing: Dispatchable now, zero solver cost, Infra family. It runs as a WARNING at intake first, not a refusal: the lookback measured the population but has not measured the false-positive rate, and a refusal calibrated on nothing would block legitimate follow-on work, which the docket does more of than it does duplicates.
gate: The check scores a candidate objective against every open and closed docket item by title and objective similarity, and separately answers whether the candidate's own citations point at a record that already contains its answer. Its threshold is frozen and committed BEFORE the retrospective replay. Replayed against the 114 closed items it reports, whatever the numbers say, how many of the 13 already-done or duplicate items it flags and how many of the other 101 it flags falsely. It ships as a warning surfaced at intake, never as a silent drop, and it is not promoted to a refusal in this item.
